title: Applications of Calculus: Maxima, Minima, and Areas

questions.question: The function f(x) = x² − 8x + 7 attains its minimum at:
questions.rationale: f′(x) = 2x − 8 = 0 gives x = 4, and f″(x) = 2 > 0 confirms a minimum there.

questions.question: At a local maximum, the sign of f′ changes from:
questions.rationale: The graph rises before the peak and falls after it, so f′ goes from positive to negative; the reverse marks a minimum.

On the interval from −2 to 2, the global minimum of f(x) = x³ − 3x is:
questions.rationale: Critical points x = ±1 plus endpoints give f(−2) = −2, f(−1) = 2, f(1) = −2, f(2) = 2; the least value is −2.

questions.question: A farmer fences a rectangle with 40 m of fencing. The largest possible area is:
questions.rationale: A(x) = x(20 − x), and A′(x) = 20 − 2x = 0 gives x = 10; the square 10 m × 10 m has area 100 m².

questions.question: An open box is made by cutting squares of side x from a 20 cm × 20 cm sheet. The volume-maximising cut is:
questions.rationale: V(x) = x(20 − 2x)², and V′ = 4(3x − 10)(x − 10) = 0 gives x = 10/3 (x = 10 collapses the box).

questions.question: The area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3 is:
questions.rationale: ∫₀³ x² dx = x³/3 evaluated from 0 to 3 = 27/3 = 9 square units.

questions.question: The area enclosed between y = x and y = x² from x = 0 to x = 1 is:
questions.rationale: ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6; subtract the curves before integrating.

questions.question: A particle moves with velocity v(t) = 3t². Its displacement from t = 0 to t = 2 is:
questions.rationale: Displacement is ∫₀² 3t² dt = t³ from 0 to 2 = 8 m.

questions.question: If f″(c) > 0 at a critical point c where f′(c) = 0, then c is:
questions.rationale: Positive second derivative means the curve bends upward — a valley — so the critical point is a local minimum.
